reasons: intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played the entire hand. All three attacks are printed at cost 0, so they are free regardless of the Spark bank, and there is only one enemy, so Rapid Fire's four random 4s all land on Seapunk for 16. Kaboom! adds 7 and Flame on the Wick adds 6, for 29 total damage, taking Seapunk from 45 to 16. That left my 2 Energy with nothing to buy except Duck and Cover, so I spent 1 on it for 5 Block, cutting the telegraphed 11-damage attack down to 6 and leaving me at 36/62. Order barely mattered: I led with Rapid Fire so the Spark consumption (which does nothing here, since the attacks already cost 0) was spent on the biggest hit rather than the smallest, in case the bank matters to any hidden interaction, and dropped Block last since incoming damage resolves after my turn either way.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Only briefly, and it did not survive: holding Duck and Cover and playing the three attacks alone. There is no reason to hold it — Energy does not carry over, the attacks are free, and there is nothing else in hand to spend the point on — so the block is strictly free value against a telegraphed attack. Beyond that, none: there is no target choice with one enemy, no Choose one, no Exhaust, and no way to spend the second Energy.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It empties the hand, so nothing is held back for a future turn — though with no retain text printed on any of these cards, holding is likely worth nothing anyway. It also leaves 1 Energy unspent, because there was no second thing to buy. And the whole line does not kill: Seapunk survives at 16 with a fresh intent I will have to face next turn with a new hand, so I traded a full hand for 29 damage and 5 Block rather than for a clean finish.
answers.q4_different_intent: Not in any way that changes what I play. If Seapunk had telegraphed a defensive or buffing move instead of the 11 attack, the 5 Block would be wasted — but Duck and Cover still costs an Energy I have no other use for, so I would play it anyway on the chance the intent is misread or a follow-up lands. A much larger attack would not change it either: 5 Block is all the mitigation this hand can produce, and every attack is free, so there is no damage-versus-defense tension to resolve. The only telegraph that would have mattered is one implying an enemy I could actually kill this turn or a multi-enemy board where Rapid Fire's random targeting became a real decision, and neither is on this page.
